cause_quote: The original share extension declared `NSExtensionActivationSupportsImageWithMaxCount` 10 in Info.plist while ShareViewController used `let maxImageAttachments = 3` and only counted videos (`_ = videoCount`) without sending them.
user_saw: iOS offered OpenClaw in the share sheet for 4+ photos or a video, but the sheet then blocked Send with 'Only 3 of 4 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.'
summary: Narrows the iOS Share extension activation rule to at most 3 images and drops the movie entry so iOS only offers OpenClaw for content the extension can send.
reasoning: Read via the GitHub commits API (pre-graft): #19424 (bfc9736) introduced the share extension with a 10-image activation rule but a 3-image send limit and no video sending; #20308 (c2d12b7e) later added NSExtensionActivationSupportsMovieWithMaxCount 1 while videos were still unsendable. Before #106513 (6e8df6c) the extra items were dropped silently; that commit made them a visible block without narrowing the activation rule. The mismatch shipped with the feature, so I classify it as never-worked with #19424 as cause; medium confidence because the video half came from #20308 and the blocked-sheet symptom from #106513.
